instruction:
Marguerite has the resolution-basis item open on the Ocotillo peer-review checklist and will not sign Phase 1 rev B until it closes.  I need a short note I can put in front of her that settles the resolution question on what is already on the file server, because nothing new is being run for this.

Tell me where the plume resolution index lands for the result the report rests on, with the cell size and the plume length scale behind it, and whether our band is met.  Then tell me what our resolution acceptance rests on, and whether anything about that basis needs a decision from Marguerite.

I also want to know whether the resolved-energy figure was taken inside the region the index describes, and whether the ambient values behind the plume length scale represent the site, and what the site's conditions would do to it.

Last, tell me whether the item can close, and if it cannot, what would settle it.

Put it in a Word note saved as /filesystem/CFDME-2025-041_resolution_note_revA.docx please.

L99: Appendix A — SOW §3.1 case matrix and boundary-condition summary
L100: Boundary-condition summary for each of the six SOW §3.1 wildfire cases (240°/270° × 5, 8, 12 m/s at 20 ft), including wind-inlet reference height, roughness length, ambient temperature, and relative humidity from the site envelope in §5.1.

L49: Fire-source stationarity. The 3.0 m front segment is held stationary within the LES sub-domain; the wall assembly is at the point of nearest approach for the sampled interval. Fire-front advance across the assembly footprint is not simulated within the sub-domain.
L50: Meteorological stationarity. Inlet wind speed and direction are stationary within each case at the values in the SOW §3.1 matrix; diurnal, gust, and synoptic-scale variability are represented only by the envelope in §5.
L51: Cavity contents. The cavity is modelled as open air with no insulation, per the as-built assembly.
L52: Concrete properties. Printed siliceous-aggregate concrete properties are those in the modeling standard reference table, with temperature dependence enabled; spatial variability introduced by the printing process is not represented.

L69: The plume in every solved case exhibits a well-organised puffing signature at the plume base, with a puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz. The puffing signature is resolved in time by the transient LES; centreline temperature and velocity monitors oscillate at that frequency about their mean values, sampled over no fewer than twenty puffing cycles at t ≥ 8 s.
L70: 5.4 Thermal response — preliminary
L71: Preliminary plume-centreline peaks on the fine grid are T_peak ≈ 1461 K and U_z,peak ≈ 12.4 m/s at the reference probe location (0.75·D* above the source top surface).
